rich_summary: With the monkey search party despairing of ever crossing the ocean to find Sita, the aged Jambavan addresses Hanuman, who sits quietly apart. He reminds the army that their success depends on the one hero capable of the task and calls Hanuman forth. To awaken Hanuman’s forgotten power, Jambavan recounts his divine origin: born to Anjana through the wind‑god Vayu, blessed with immense strength, intelligence, and speed. As a child, Hanuman once leapt skyward to seize the rising sun as if it were a fruit, was struck by Indra’s thunderbolt, and afterward received boons of invulnerability and near‑immortality from the gods. Jambavan concludes by urging him to rise and cross the ocean like Vishnu striding the worlds, transforming the monkeys’ despair into hope and setting the stage for Hanuman’s legendary leap to Lanka.

highlight_spans.why: A proverb about tending the root to secure the fruit, framing Hanuman as the essential foundation of the mission.
The mythic childhood moment when Hanuman leaps toward the sun, revealing the vast scale of his latent power.
Jambavan’s climactic exhortation urging Hanuman to rise and cross the ocean like Vishnu striding the worlds.

top_scenes.scene_text: Young Hanuman rockets into the sky toward the blazing rising sun, mistaking it for a fruit, while the heavens blaze around him.
Indra hurls the thunderbolt at the airborne child Hanuman as he streaks across the sky toward the sun.
The aged bear‑king Jambavan stands before the vast monkey host, pointing toward the ocean as he calls on Hanuman to rise and leap across it.
